unit.why: A short anecdote about the pre-Hasidic halakhist R. Falk Kohen (author of the Sma), who lost a lawsuit in which his own book's ruling applied, told to illustrate the rabbinic dictum that no one sees fault in himself.
unit.boundary_note: The division ends with '(ס׳ י״מ) : מענין אכילה', a source reference and the topic heading of the next item; the heading belongs to the next division.

stories.start_quote: והנה שמעתי דבר הפלא ממגידי אמת
stories.end_quote: שאמרו אין אדם רואה חובה לעצמו וכו׳
stories.summary_en: R. Falk Kohen, author of the Sma, has a lawsuit and is ordered to pay 22,000. He is shown that his own book rules this way on such a case, marvels at himself, and affirms the sages' saying that no one sees fault in himself.

tags.why: Anecdote about an earlier, non-Hasidic rabbinic authority, the Sma.
